question: Can samples of one conventional mineral species remain different under a formation-history identity regime, and what evidence supports that distinction?

evidenceLayers.role: native sample identifier, age, locality, stratigraphy, and material description
95 retained in-situ LA-ICP-MS rows with source columns and reported uncertainties
three bounded sample-specific growth interpretations, each with an exact article locator
one conventional FeS2 species label used only as the species-level comparison key
regime-relative classes, unresolved mappings, and explicit non-claims

identityRegimes.meaning: All ten selected records are pyrite samples in the bounded source cohort.
The ten physical sample records remain distinct regardless of species equality.
Three representative samples have bounded published profiles; seven are deliberately not mapped by this release.

formationClaims.locator: Figure 1 caption, lines 733-745 in the accepted manuscript text
formationClaims.evidenceSummary: Little trace-element variation across the nodule and minor sulfur-isotope change at its margins support predominantly pervasive growth with minor later pyrite production at the margin.

formationClaims.locator: Figure 2 caption, lines 746-757 in the accepted manuscript text
formationClaims.evidenceSummary: Spatial changes in trace elements and sulfur isotopes are interpreted as predominantly concentric growth.

formationClaims.locator: Section 5 discussion of Figure 3, lines 352-359 in the accepted manuscript text
formationClaims.evidenceSummary: Low variation and fine grains in the centre are interpreted as many early nucleation sites; later diagenetic pyrite filled space toward the margin.

historicalLoad.reason: The sources do not define a finite universe of admissible formation paths, transition costs, or a history-free counterfactual baseline. Undefined must not be displayed as zero.

nonClaims: The ten samples are not a complete pyrite, sedimentary-pyrite, or mineral-formation space.
A common pyrite species label does not establish sample identity.
Age, locality, formation name, or description alone does not establish a growth mechanism.
LA-ICP-MS values are observations and do not automatically become formation classifications.
The three formation profiles remain qualified interpretations from the cited article.
The seven unmapped samples are unresolved only within this bounded reviewed mapping, not globally unknowable.
No sulfur-isotope numeric series is reconstructed from article figures.
Duplicate Pb_Py workbook headings are retained by source column and are not assigned invented isotope labels.
The case does not replace IMA-style conventional mineral species classification.
No Onto2D-generated causal relation is added to the source graph.
Historical Load is undefined because no finite path universe and cost model are declared.
